agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Diffusion stage, mechanisms and bounded timing implications

analytical_question: Does the sponsor claim that 33.9% broad AI use and 40% agent scaling establish irreversible chart-agent chasm crossing, early-majority peer status and urgent rollout?
general_et_finding: The sponsor inference is not supported. S2 measures any AI use in Finance and Insurance during a particular 2026 snapshot; S1 measures agent scaling in any function among a multinational large-revenue respondent subgroup. Different innovations, populations, denominators, dates and adoption criteria make 33.9% and 40% non-combinable. No evidence identifies a Rogers adopter curve for agentic AI in comparable financial firms. General provisional stage: organizational experimentation and some reported scaling, but exact adopter category unknown. Vendors can act as change agents, and peer testimonials as opinion leadership; neither is independently verified here.
application_finding: No observation establishes chart-to-source checking uptake, much less durable early-majority installation. Relative advantage (saved review time), compatibility (existing BI and human ownership), complexity (multistep agent error and source access), trialability (isolated synthetic sandbox) and observability (audited correction logs) are testable hypotheses, not scored outcomes. Rogers knowledge/persuasion signals exist at the technology level; decision to study is not production implementation or confirmation of this application. Vendor wording such as “useful, not new” is a persuasion frame, not a count of adopters or demonstrated utility.
organization_specific_finding: The hypothetical firm is conservative and has no implemented chart agent or measured savings. Its synthetic/public-data sandbox can support four-week learning, while live enterprise information and external production models remain unapproved. Its peer percentile is unidentifiable: mid-sized is not S1’s revenue classification, and S2 is broad sector AI. Financial-reporting errors and disclosure risks constrain interpretation and timing, not general technology prevalence. An aggressive stance would change willingness to trial, not justify reinterpreting either survey.

evidence.claim: Agent scaling in at least one function: 40% among respondents in report-defined large-revenue group versus 27% previous survey; smaller group 22%.
evidence.source_or_reference: S1: McKinsey, The state of AI in 2026, agent-use discussion/Exhibit 2
evidence.notes: 1,719 respondents across 97 nations; neither firm census nor chart-review application count.

evidence.claim: Finance and Insurance AI use in any business function 33.9%, versus national 19.8%.
evidence.source_or_reference: S2: US Census, Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
evidence.notes: Not agent scaling; November 2025 wording break; cannot infer chart-agent penetration.

evidence.claim: Rogers categories, five attributes, diffusion process, influence actors, 16% heuristic.
evidence.source_or_reference: C1: ET Module 6 The Diffusion of Emerging Technologies FA25, slides 18-29, 32-35, 40-54, 58-63
evidence.notes: Heuristics are not measurements of this use case or peer social system.

evidence.claim: Model-directed tools create flexible multi-step behavior but entail complexity, costs and compounding-error risk.
evidence.notes: Design mechanism, not independent diffusion or performance evidence.

evidence.claim: MCP specifies model-to-tool connectivity with consent/security considerations.
evidence.notes: Potential ecosystem accelerator, not proof of adoption or compatibility.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Claim failure 1: S2 33.9% is broad AI sector usage, not agentic chart checking; November 2025 wording changed.
Claim failure 2: S1 40% is self-reported agent scaling for large-revenue respondents across functions and geographies, not mid-sized US financial peers.
Claim failure 3: 16% is a conceptual threshold for a defined adopter population, not a numerical test across unmatched surveys; neither irreversibility nor urgency follows.
No verified installed base, retention, comparable peer denominator or vendor-performance measurements exist.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that the claimed inference is invalid on scope/denominator grounds; low confidence in any numerical chart-review diffusion-stage estimate. Actual agentic AI diffusion is broader than this application, but exact stage and permanence remain unverified.
value_opportunity_implication: A synthetic read-only chart-review experiment could measure potential time reduction and observable correction quality. These are opportunities to learn, not evidence of ROI, competitive lag or vendor-promised readiness.
risk_governance_implication: Do not translate sponsor urgency into production authority. Require analyst approval, audit trails, and security review; keep production information and external production-model use off limits under the scenario. Agent error compounding (S3) and connector consent/security (S4) are material mechanisms.
recommendation_management_implication: Reject the specific crossing/early-majority/urgent-rollout claim, not the possibility of studying the technology. Provisional timing: four-week sandbox evidence collection and quarterly reassessment for a year; no full rollout verdict. Evaluate 16% only with matched innovation, social system, denominator, implementation definition and longitudinal observations.
change_monitoring_triggers: End of four weeks: measured discrepancy detection, false alarms, review time, reproducibility and source lineage on approved synthetic cases.
Quarterly: verified comparable-peer chart-agent active adoption, sustained use and consistent survey definitions.
Documented change in production permissions, governance safeguards, connector behavior or independent efficacy evidence.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Cannot assert an irreversible chasm crossing, early-majority peer placement, or urgency of rollout.
Need identified population and adopter definition, longitudinal peer installations, local measured performance, and verified production controls.
